{{Use mdy dates|date=July 2025}}
'''Bruce Buzzell Benson'''<ref name=asteria>{{cite web|url=http://asteria.fivecolleges.edu/findaids/amherst/ma01016.html|title=Bruce B. Benson (AC 1943) Papers, 1939–1988|publisher=Asteria Archives|accessdate=October 2, 2019}}</ref> (1922–1990) was a professor of physics at the [[Amherst College]].

Benson was born in [[Choteau, Montana]]. He was a graduate of [[Amherst College]] and then got his master's and Ph.D. degrees from [[Yale University]] where he later served as an instructor from 1944 to 1946. In 1947, Benson returned to his alma mater to join its faculty. From 1957 to 1967 he was an associate professor of physics at the [[Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution]] and from 1977 to 1990 served as an associate editor of the journal ''[[Marine Chemistry]]''. During his time as professor of physics at Amherst, he worked closely with [[Daniel Krause]], studying [[thermodynamics]] of the [[Solubility|solubilities]] of gases. Benson died of [[respiratory failure]] on March 7, 1990 at [[Cooley Dickinson Hospital]], [[Northampton, Massachusetts]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Bruce B. Benson, 68, A Professor of Physics|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=March 10, 1990|page=10}}</ref>

Benson's wife, [[Lucy W. Benson|Lucy Wilson Benson]], was involved with local liberal politics of the time, and was a president of the [[League of Women Voters]].  Bruce Benson joined the League of Women Voters, too, and was reportedly its first male member.  Lucy Benson served as [[United States Secretary of Health and Human Services|U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services]] as well as [[Under Secretary of State for Arms Control and International Security Affairs]].<ref name=asteria/>

Seven years after Benson's death, Harry V. Keefe, a former roommate of Benson, donated the Keefe Science Library to Amherst in his honor.<ref name=asteria/>
